answer: To deter sybil farms that spread like a vine, an agent market can make each account store a unique 80 GB disk sector salted with a saffron seed hash and pass random byte audit reads in 6 ms or burn 100% of its lock bond. One honest agent uses 80 GB of local SSD space costing $1 monthly and serves checks like a steady jetty. Operating 1,000 fake accounts pushes an attacker into a linear cost of 80 TB on fast drives at $4,200 per month, since rebuilding slices misses the 6 ms cutoff. This fails if flash storage becomes nearly free or loose latency rules hide remote reads.
